q: How tall is Mount Everest above sea level?
note: China and Nepal jointly announced 8,848.86 m in 2020.

q: How far is the Moon from Earth, on average?
note: The average distance between the centres of Earth and the Moon is about 384,400 km: roughly 30 Earths side by side.

q: How many keys does a standard modern piano have?
note: 52 white keys and 36 black ones, spanning a little over seven octaves.

q: How many ways can a deck of 52 playing cards be shuffled?
note: 52! is about 8 × 10^67: a well-shuffled deck is almost certainly in an order no deck has ever been in before.

q: How tall is the Statue of Liberty from the ground to the tip of the torch?
note: About 93 m (305 ft) including the pedestal; the copper statue itself is 46 m.

q: How many Earths could fit inside Jupiter, by volume?
note: About 1,321 Earths, yet the Sun could hold about a thousand Jupiters.

q: How many member states does the United Nations have?
note: South Sudan, in 2011, was the most recent country to join.

q: How much blood is in a typical adult human body?
note: About 5 litres, and your heart pumps roughly that much every minute at rest.

q: In roughly what year did Gutenberg print his Bible?
note: Printed around 1454–1455 in Mainz. About 49 copies survive, at least in part.

q: How many minutes does the International Space Station take to orbit Earth once?
note: About 93 minutes: the crew sees around 16 sunrises a day.

q: How much area does the Amazon rainforest cover?
note: About 5.5 million km², spread across nine countries.

q: How far does light travel in one year?
note: About 9.46 trillion km: one light-year.

q: How fast does light travel in a vacuum?
note: Exactly 299,792,458 m/s: the metre is defined by it.

q: At roughly what altitude does the International Space Station orbit?
note: About 400 km up: roughly the distance from London to Paris, but straight up.

q: How many bones are in an adult human skeleton?
note: Babies are born with around 270; many fuse as we grow.

q: How many seconds does sunlight take to reach Earth?
note: About 8 minutes and 19 seconds: the Sun you see is the Sun of eight minutes ago.

q: How old is the Earth?
note: Radiometric dating of meteorites puts Earth at about 4.54 billion years old.

q: How big is the Sahara desert?
note: About 9.2 million km², close to the size of China or the United States.

q: What is the diameter of the Moon?
note: About 3,474 km: a bit more than a quarter of Earth's.

q: What is the total volume of Earth's oceans?
note: About 1.335 billion cubic kilometres of water.

q: How long is the Nile river?
note: Usually given as 6,650 km, though measuring rivers is famously contested: some surveys make the Amazon longer.

q: How long is the main span of the Golden Gate Bridge?
note: 4,200 feet: the longest suspension bridge span in the world when it opened in 1937.

q: Roughly how many languages are spoken in the world today?
note: Estimates are around 7,000, and about 40% of them are endangered.

q: How long is Earth's equator?
note: The equator is 40,075 km around. The metre was once defined so the pole-to-equator distance would be 10,000 km.

q: How many base pairs are in the human genome?
note: About 3.1 billion base pairs, roughly 750 megabytes of information.

q: How deep is Lake Baikal, the world's deepest lake?
note: 1,642 m deep, and it holds about 22% of the world's fresh surface water.

q: How many seconds are in a (non-leap) year?
note: 365 × 24 × 60 × 60 = 31,536,000. A handy approximation: π × 10 million.

q: How many IPv4 addresses are there?
note: 2 to the power 32, about 4.3 billion: fewer than there are people, which is why IPv6 exists.

q: Roughly how many different possible games of chess are there? (Answer in powers of ten if you like: 1e30 means a 1 with 30 zeros.)
note: Claude Shannon estimated the game-tree complexity of chess at about 10^120, far more than atoms in the observable universe.

q: How tall is the Burj Khalifa in Dubai?
note: The tallest building in the world since 2009.

q: In what year was the Taj Mahal's main mausoleum completed?
note: The mausoleum was completed in 1643; work on the whole complex went on for another decade.

q: What is the area of the Pacific Ocean?
note: About 165 million km²: larger than all of Earth's land put together.

q: How far away is Proxima Centauri, the nearest star after the Sun?
note: About 4.24 light-years: around 40 trillion km.

q: Roughly how many human cells make up an adult body?
note: A 2013 estimate put it at about 37.2 trillion cells, not counting the bacteria that live in and on us.

q: How much does an adult human brain weigh?
note: About 1.2 to 1.4 kg: around 2% of body weight, but it uses about 20% of the body's energy.

q: What is the diameter of the Sun?
note: About 1.39 million km: 109 Earths across.

q: What is the maximum takeoff weight of an Airbus A380?
note: 575 tonnes: the heaviest passenger airliner ever built.

q: In what year was Mount Everest first summited?
note: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reached the top on 29 May 1953.

q: How many neurons are in the human brain?
note: The usual estimate is about 86 billion neurons.

q: How tall was the Great Pyramid of Giza when it was built?
note: Originally 146.6 m. It was the tallest human-made structure in the world for nearly 4,000 years.

q: How tall is Hyperion, the tallest known living tree?
note: A coast redwood in California, about 116 m tall. Its exact location is kept secret to protect it.

q: How many vertebrae are in a giraffe's neck?
note: Seven, the same as yours: each one is just up to 25 cm long.

q: How many transistors are on Apple's M1 chip?
note: 16 billion transistors on a chip about 120 mm².

q: How many litres of water does an Olympic swimming pool hold (50 m × 25 m × 2 m)?
note: 2.5 million litres at the minimum 2 m depth.

q: How tall is Angel Falls in Venezuela, the world's highest waterfall?
note: 979 m, with an uninterrupted drop of 807 m.

q: What is the area of Russia?
note: About 17.1 million km²: more than an eighth of Earth's inhabited land.

q: If you stretched out the DNA in one human cell, how long would it be?
note: About 2 metres, packed into a nucleus a few micrometres across.

q: How old is the universe?
note: Measurements of the cosmic microwave background put it at about 13.8 billion years.

q: What is Earth's average radius?
note: About 6,371 km from the centre to the surface; the equator bulges about 21 km further out than the poles.

q: What is the area of Vatican City?
note: About 0.49 km² (49 hectares): the smallest sovereign state in the world.

q: How deep is the Challenger Deep, the deepest known point in the ocean?
note: About 10,935 m: if Everest sat at the bottom, its peak would still be over 2 km underwater.

q: How tall is the Eiffel Tower, including its antennas?
note: 330 m. In hot weather the iron expands and it grows by up to 15 cm.

q: What is the wingspan of a Boeing 747-400?
note: 64.4 m: longer than the Wright brothers' first flight (36.6 m).

q: How many people have walked on the Moon?
note: Twelve astronauts on six Apollo missions, between 1969 and 1972.

q: How far is the Earth from the Sun, on average?
note: One astronomical unit is defined as exactly 149,597,870,700 metres: about 150 million km.

q: What is the average depth of the ocean?
note: About 3.7 km. The deepest point, the Challenger Deep, is nearly three times deeper.

q: How fast does Earth move around the Sun?
note: About 29.78 km/s, or over 107,000 km/h: in the minute it takes to read this, you have travelled about 1,800 km around the Sun.

q: How long was the RMS Titanic?
note: 269.1 m (882 ft 9 in) overall.

q: How many positions can a Rubik's Cube be in?
note: About 43 quintillion, yet every one can be solved in 20 moves or fewer.

q: How many transistors were on the Intel 4004, the first commercial microprocessor (1971)?
note: 2,300 transistors. Fifty years later chips hold tens of billions.

q: How fast does sound travel through air at 20 °C?
note: About 343 metres per second, or one kilometre in roughly three seconds: count after the lightning.

q: How long is the Great Wall of China, counting all its branches?
note: A 2012 Chinese survey measured all the walls built over two millennia at 21,196 km.
